transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-05
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration (mins): 48
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Beacon ML Eng), Rajesh Patel (Beacon CTO), Sophie Duarte (Beacon Product)

Summary (auto):
Quick Optimize console demo focused on INT8 vs FP8 precision profiles, decision path for speed vs fidelity, and how fallback rules / canary rollouts work. Agreed next steps: share pricing, spin up sandbox, run benchmark with customer's prompts.

Resources shared:
- Deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/optimize-demo
- Benchmark sheet (customer sandbox): https://redwood.app/workspaces/beacon/benchmarks
- Sandbox: https://sandbox.redwood.com/beacon

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. Ethan and I will run through a short Optimize walkthrough — specifically how we think about int eight versus F P eight — sorry FP8 — and how you can pick a profile for production.
[00:18] Rajesh: Great thanks, we've had some internal debate — latency is critical for a subset of endpoints, cost matters, and of course we need to keep clinical fidelity for diagnostic triage.
[00:30] Ethan: Totally, that's exactly the tradeoff we're going to show. We'll start with the console demo, show a couple of pre-built quantization profiles, then run a quick sandbox benchmark and show the quality delta for your prompt set.
[00:45] Laura: Quick Q — when you say "profile" do you mean quantization per-layer? Or whole-model presets?
[00:52] Ethan: Good question. In Optimize the profile can be a model-wide preset or an advanced per-layer override. Most teams start with profiles we call "fidelity-lane" and "speed-lane" and then tune specific layers if needed.
[01:10] Sophie: Are there any safety checks — like if we push an INT8 profile will Redwood auto-fallback if quality regresses?
[01:18] Maya: Yes, we have built-in rollout policies. You can do a canary that routes 5% of traffic, monitor quality metrics (we hook to your eval set), and automatic fallback to a higher-precision variant if we detect a regression beyond your configured threshold.
[01:34] Rajesh: That sounds good. On security: we need SOC2 plus KMS integration, and data never leaving our VPC during POC. Is that supported for the sandbox?
[01:43] Maya: For the sandbox we can do a VPC-peered playground for Dedicated or Private deployments. For hosted sandbox the data is ephemeral; we'll share the KMS integration guide and SOC2 cert — Ethan will drop the link.
[01:55] Ethan: (link) — sending now. Also note that for on-prem / private we support HSM-backed keys through our KMS integrations.
[02:05] Speaker 6: [crosstalk]
[02:12] Ethan: Jumping into the console — you should see the Optimize tab, the pre-built profiles on the left. I'm switching to the "speed-lane" profile to show its inference config: INT8 quantization, block-quantize for attention and MLP, aggressive KV cache reuse and continuous batching.
[02:35] [02:35] Ethan: Running a quick dry-run benchmark against a 50-sample subset of Beacon's prompts (we uploaded the set earlier).
[02:45] Ethan: I'm seeing median latency drop from ~220ms to ~95ms on the G5-like instance in the sandbox with the speed-lane. Tokens per second increases by ~2.3x, cost estimate reduces by ~58% for the same throughput.
[03:05] Laura: Those numbers are promising, but what's the quality impact? A drop of 8-10% in Rouge/BLEU style metrics might be fine for summaries, but not acceptable for triage decisions.
[03:18] Ethan: Right — here's where we compare side-by-side. Switching to the fidelity-lane (FP8 hybrid) you get median latency ~150ms and quality metrics close to baseline fp16 — usually within 1-2% on our downstream evals.
[03:36] Maya: To be clear, FP8 in our runtime is the newer per-tensor FP8 path (we call it "FP8 hybrid") that preserves higher dynamic range for sensitive layers — so quality is much better than naive conversion.
[03:48] Rajesh: Do you have logs of hallucination rates or specific clinical metric? We don't use Rouge heavily, we use a precision/recall style evaluation for entity extraction.
[03:58] Ethan: Yep, you can bring your own evals. In the Evaluate tab we mapped your entity-extraction script — you can plug in a webhook or upload results. When we ran your 50-sample script earlier the entity-extraction F1 dropped 0.7% on FP8 hybrid and 3.9% on INT8 speed-lane.
[04:18] Laura: 3.9% is rough but maybe tolerable for low-risk endpoints. For high-risk ones we'll keep fidelity-lane.
[04:28] Sophie: Walk me through how we'd implement a rollout. We can't flip everyone at once.
[04:33] Ethan: The Console has a rollout wizard. Step 1: create a deployment with both variants (fidelity, speed). Step 2: set traffic split — we recommend 95/5 initial. Step 3: configure quality checks — choose your eval set and thresholds (e.g., F1 drop >1% triggers alert). Step 4: define automatic remediation — rollback to fidelity or route to Dedicated fallback.
[04:56] Maya: And the Canary logs are surfaced in Console and in the tracing pane; you can export token-level traces if you want to debug a failure.
[05:06] Rajesh: About Dedicated fallback — is that a separate instance pool or just a higher-precision model on same infra?
[05:13] Ethan: It can be either. Fallback policy can point to a different model artifact (fp16) on the same pool or a Dedicated pool. Many enterprise customers point fallback to a Dedicated reserved capacity so they hit latency SLAs even under regression.
[05:30] [05:30] Laura: Can you demo the automatic fallback?
[05:33] Ethan: I can simulate it — toggling the threshold so the speed-lane fails the eval and triggers rollback.
[05:38] [05:38] Ethan: Ok simulate run... injecting a synthetic failure into the eval webhook. You should see the rollout instantly flag as breached and traffic snaps back to fidelity-lane.
[05:50] Sophie: Nice, that gives us confidence to try a small production rollout.
[05:54] Maya: One other nuance — quantization sensitivity varies by prompt length and token distribution. Short prompts sometimes show smaller degradation; long clinical notes with long-range dependencies can be more sensitive. We recommend stratified evals (by prompt length and task).
[06:15] Rajesh: What's the effort to tune per-layer? We don't want to hire someone full-time to micromanage it.
[06:20] Ethan: The Console has an auto-suggest flow. It runs a sensitivity sweep (we call it a quant-scan) across layers and suggests the minimal number of layer overrides to hit your quality constraints. For most workloads we get a good profile in 2–4 passes.
[06:36] Laura: Is that the q-scan that produced the "hybrid-lite" profile in your earlier emails?
[06:41] Ethan: Exactly. Hybrid-lite is typically FP8 for attention and INT8 for MLP, with a few high-sensitivity layers pinned to FP16. It's a common win.
[06:52] Rajesh: Can we set cost targets as well? Like, I want cost reduction >= 40% but quality delta < 1%.
[06:58] Maya: Yes, Optimize supports multi-objective constraints. You can specify cost reduction target and a quality floor; the optimizer will propose a profile that tries to meet both. If no profile meets them it shows a pareto front and we can choose manually.
[07:15] [07:15] Ethan: I'm sharing the benchmark sheet in chat — you'll see the run we did: baseline fp16, fp8 hybrid, int8 speed-lane, plus an intermediate "safe-speed" profile.
[07:25] Laura: I see it. In the sheet the safe-speed has a 45% cost reduction and 0.9% F1 drop — that might be our sweet spot.
[07:34] Sophie: How does this interact with caching — you mentioned KV cache earlier?
[07:38] Ethan: Right — we do prefix caching and persistent KV reuse where possible; the effective latency gain can be larger for conversational workloads because we reuse previous KV states. For single-shot long prompts the gains are mostly from quantization. Note that KV cache name sometimes comes through in transcripts as "K V cash" — minor transcription artifact.
[07:55] Rajesh: On infra — which instance families did you run these on? G5? A100?
[08:01] Ethan: In the sandbox we used a G5-like profile; for Dedicated we support A100 and H100 pools. Performance numbers vary — for H100 the latency dropped less percentual but absolute tps went up because of bigger batch capacity.
[08:18] Laura: Any known model-architecture gotchas? We use a 30B LLM with some custom adapters.
[08:24] Ethan: Larger models sometimes have layers that are extremely sensitivity-critical — adapter layers especially. We recommend including a small set of adapter-heavy prompts in the eval. Also if you use LoRA, we preserve LoRA deltas — quantization is applied to base weights.
[08:38] Rajesh: For data residency — if we run Private on-prem, do you still provide the Console?
[08:43] Maya: Yes, Private comes with a customer-controlled control plane; you can run the Console in VPC or self-host it. We provide the observability stack as a containerized bundle.
[08:53] Sophie: Ok, digging into the sheet — there's a column for "regression examples". Can you show how we triage one?
[08:59] Ethan: Sure — clicking an example: the token-level diff highlights a hallucinated entity that appears only in INT8. We can export that snippet and run a targeted per-layer sweep to find which layer caused it.
[09:14] Laura: How long does a per-layer sweep take? We have time constraints.
[09:19] Ethan: For a 30B model it's usually a couple hours full sweep in our sandbox, but the Console supports incremental sweeps and early stopping once you've got acceptable metrics. If you're in a rush we can run a targeted scan on the top 20 most sensitive layers.
[09:34] [09:34] Rajesh: On cost and pricing — can you give a quick breakdown between hosted and Dedicated?
[09:38] Maya: Hosted: pay-as-you-go per-token + optional Optimize add-on. Dedicated: committed monthly capacity with lower per-token and predictable latency; reserved nodes for SLA. We sent a pricing example in the deck. I'll include a Dedicated worksheet with different commit levels.
[09:54] Sophie: Do you have references in healthcare customers using FP8 hybrid in production?
[09:59] Maya: Yes, a couple of HIPAA-adjacent customers are in production with hybrid profiles; I can get you anonymized case metrics.
[10:08] Laura: For the POC, what's the recommended success criteria?
[10:12] Ethan: We typically propose: 1) achieve >40% cost reduction on targeted endpoints, 2) F1/precision/recall regression <1% on eval set, 3) end-to-end 95th pct latency < 200ms for critical endpoints. If those are hit we sign off and move to Dedicated.
[10:28] Rajesh: Timeline — we want POC started in 1 week if possible.
[10:32] Maya: We can spin the sandbox and tests in 48–72 hours after we get the prompt set and access.
[10:39] Sophie: One more operational question: how do you version profiles and rollbacks — is there an audit trail for compliance?
[10:46] Ethan: Yes, profiles are versioned in the Console, each rollout records an immutable audit event — who triggered it, the eval artifacts used, and the exact model artifact ids. Those can be exported for audits.
[10:58] [10:58] Laura: I'm scanning the benchmark sheet — curious about tokenization differences. You mentioned tokenization can change effective cost.
[11:05] Ethan: Yeah, tokenization differences can shift token counts; we normalize cost per-character and per-token in the sheet so you can inspect both. For clinical text with lots of punctuation the tokenization overhead is higher.
[11:18] Rajesh: Are there licensing implications for model artifacts? We use a community model forked from an open repo.
[11:24] Maya: We do model vetting as part of onboarding. As long as the license allows commercial use and redistribution to your Dedicated pool, we're fine. We'll list the model hash and provenance in the onboarding doc.
[11:36] Sophie: Ok, let's talk POC scope — can we do 3 endpoints: triage, summary, and medication extraction?
[11:42] Maya: Sounds reasonable; we'll target triage+med extraction first for quant-sensitivity because they're higher risk.
[11:50] Ethan: For med extraction we recommend keeping the fidelity-lane until we've validated the hybrid profile on a 500-sample eval.
[11:58] Laura: 500 samples is doable. We'll prioritize that.
[12:02] [12:02] Ethan: Demo note — sometimes transcripts show product names slightly off, e.g., "Optimize" becomes "opt my size" in auto transcribe; ignore that.
[12:12] Sophie: (laugh) noted.
[12:15] Maya: Wrapping up — agreed next steps?
[12:18] Rajesh: Laura will provide the prompts and traffic profile. Rajesh will confirm the security contacts. Sophie will sign off on the three endpoints for POC.
[12:27] Maya: From Redwood we'll share pricing + Dedicated worksheet, the benchmark runbook and sandbox link, and a short onboarding checklist.
[12:34] Laura: One last question — can we do a side-by-side A/B of different quant engines? I've seen other vendors have different INT8 algorithms.
[12:43] Ethan: Yes, Optimize supports comparing multiple quant engines — we currently offer Redwood native INT8, OpenINT8 (third-party), and an experimental mixed FP8 path. The Console will show per-engine pareto charts.
[12:56] Rajesh: Perfect. That helps.
[13:00] Maya: Ok we'll aim to deliver the items in the next 48–72 hours. Thanks everyone.

End of recording.
